removedCopy.reason: WAVE 3A / P-1 (DEF-007) — CORRECTED IN PLACE, not removed. This was the Select option label on the discount-code kind picker. It instructed the admin to TYPE a fraction ("0.10 = 10%"), which is exactly the convention the owner's 2026-08-09 ruling reversed for the input side: storage stays FRACTIONAL, but ADMIN INPUT is percent-as-written (type 100, store 1.0). The amount field beside this label now takes percent-as-written and converts to the stored fraction (client/src/lib/percentDisplay.ts parsePercentInputToFraction), so leaving the old label in place would have told the admin to type 0.10 into a field that reads it as 0.1% — a 100x under-charge. Replaced by "Percent (type 10 for 10%)" plus an explicit on-screen convention note (data-testid=discount-percent-convention). No control, option or capability was removed: all three discount kinds are still selectable.
removedCopy.approvedBy: Ozan (owner ruling 2026-08-09 — spec/PERCENT_POLICY_v2.md, spec/00_SHARED_STANDARDS.md §1.1; WAVE 3A build directive)

MODIFICATION, NOT A REMOVAL. The refund Button, its data-testid (button-refund-invoice-<id>), its disabled logic, its label and its refund.mutate call are all still present and unchanged. ONE LINE INSIDE the onClick changed: the confirmation dialog rendered the amount by dividing minor units by 100, which UNDERSTATES A JPY REFUND BY 100x (JPY is ISO-4217 exponent 0). It now calls formatMinor(inv.amountMinor, inv.currency). This is the confirm dialog on a screen whose own copy reads 'This moves real money and cannot be undone' - the admin was shown the wrong figure before authorising a refund. PROOF OF NON-REMOVAL: reverting that single line restores 'no silent drops' with nothing else changed (Wave 21 ran this revert-and-restore). ROOT CAUSE: the guard fingerprints handlers by EXPRESSION HASH, so any edit to a handler body is indistinguishable from deleting it - the same fingerprinting weakness Wave 11 fixed for CHILD MEMBERSHIP (adding a tab read as removing the tab list) and that blocked Wave 4B from adding a roster column. The expression case is still unfixed and is logged as a guard follow-up. Allowlisting this one entry beats shipping a known 100x money-display defect on a refund dialog.

WAVE 58 / owner ruling R27 — A RELOCATION ENTRY, WITH ITS DESTINATION NAMED. DESTINATION ID: client/src/pages/founder/RoundNew.tsx	Input	onChange	expr:<the handler on data-testid="addon-pool-percent">, in the same file, in the same section (data-testid="addon-pool-section"), reachable in the browser. WHAT THIS IDENTITY WAS: the inline onChange on the "Pool size (shares)" input — `e => setAddonPoolDraft(d => ({ ...d, poolSize: e.target.value }))`. R27 rules that the option pool is entered as a PERCENTAGE of fully diluted and that "the share count becomes the derived output, shown to the founder, NEVER the input". The share count input therefore has no writer any more: it is `readOnly` and displays the derived value. Its onChange is not suppressed or stubbed out — a dead handler would be a dead promise — it is genuinely gone, and the write it performed now happens on the percentage field. WHAT IS *NOT* REMOVED, all verified by the guard census in the same run: the control itself (data-testid="addon-pool-size") is STILL ON SCREEN; its label text "Pool size (shares)" is UNCHANGED and still in the copy inventory; its container (data-testid="addon-pool-fields") and the toggle (data-testid="addon-pool-toggle") are unchanged; the wire key `poolSize` is unchanged, still sent on the `option_pool` child-round payload and still a SHARE COUNT there; and the four CardContent panel-membership records that a first attempt at this change did drop (inner=Input#24, Label#46, input#5, label#5) were RESTORED by keeping the relocated JSX lexically inside the card rather than hoisting it into a variable. This is the ONLY identity in any class that this wave could not carry across, and the file gains many more than it loses. NOTE FOR RATIFICATION: R27 authorises the percentage input and the derived share count explicitly, and its binding constraints require that a guard-identity change be "a relocation entry naming its destination, submitted for ratification — never a quiet allowlist growth". This entry is that submission. It grows scripts/silent-drop-guard/allowlist.json from 40 to 41 and is APPENDED AT THE END of its class array as a sibling, never inserted mid-list (a mid-list insertion once invalidated 46 child identities). It is NOT ratified until the owner says so.
removedEvents.approvedBy: SUBMITTED FOR RATIFICATION — owner ruling R27 (spec/OWNER_RULINGS_2026_08_13.md, 2026-08-15): "make it a percentage"; "the share count becomes the derived output, shown to the founder, never the input". R27 authorises the change that causes this identity to move but does not itself name this identity, so this entry is flagged rather than treated as pre-approved.

removedButtons.reason: WAVE 40 / F-1 — RELOCATION OF A CONTROL, NOT A SUBTRACTION OF ONE. This id exists only because the extractor records any element with role="button" as a button (extract-inventory.ts: BUTTON_TAGS.has(tag) || role === "button"), and the SPV card carried role="button" tabIndex={0}. That nesting was the proven cause of the live F-1 defect: the card's own onKeyDown fires on Enter/Space BUBBLED FROM ANY DESCENDANT, so pressing Enter on one of the 16 SPV tab triggers toggled selectedId and unmounted the entire tab panel mid-activation (reproduced in Chromium, both poles — build_log/WAVE40_REPORT.md), and role="button" additionally makes the whole subtree presentational in the accessibility tree, hiding all 16 role="tab" triggers, the publish Button and both Links from assistive tech. NOTHING WAS REMOVED: the Card keeps its data-testid, its onClick and its onKeyDown byte-identical (both event fingerprints are unchanged in this run), so click-anywhere-to-expand still works; and the disclosure gained a REAL native control appended at the end of the header column, <button data-testid=`spv-row-toggle-${s.id}`> with aria-expanded/aria-controls, which the browser activates on Enter and Space. The guard has no relocation/rename mechanism, so a role move can only be expressed as one removed id — enumeration of the four fingerprint classes shows 1 is the minimum possible loss for any fix that removes the interactive-role nesting. scripts/reachability/reachability_gate.ts rule R3 now fails the build if an interactive role is ever wrapped around these controls again. RECOMMENDED FOR WAVE 41: give the guard a `relocations` map so a control moving between elements needs no removal entry.
